aspects.says: Optional.get() on an empty Optional throws NoSuchElementException with no context; orElseThrow with an exception that names the key tells on-call what failed.
basis: section:Optional Is a Return Type, and get() Without a Check Only Renames the NullPointerException

aspects.says: orElseThrow() without arguments (Java 10) and isEmpty() (Java 11) don't exist in Java 8.
basis: section:Optional Is a Return Type, and get() Without a Check Only Renames the NullPointerException
aspects.reason: a compile-time fact about an older API; the graded runner compiles for Java 21

aspects.says: Java 8's new defaults reach classes written before them; a class that inherits List's and Set's spliterator() defaults no longer compiles until it overrides the method.
basis: section:The JDK's New Defaults Reach Classes Written Before Them, and Two of Them Can Collide

aspects.says: Methods Java 8 added, such as HashMap.merge and ArrayList.removeIf, need not call a subclass's put or remove, so a subclass that guards its mutators must override them too or wrap the collection.
basis: section:A Method Java 8 Added to a Collection Need Not Go Through Your Overrides

aspects.says: A default method can't override equals, hashCode or toString.
basis: section:Static Interface Methods Belong to the Interface: Implementers Don't Inherit Them
aspects.reason: a compile-time rule with no wrong solution that compiles

aspects.says: An Optional field makes a Serializable class fail at run time with NotSerializableException; keep the field nullable and return Optional from the getter.
basis: section:An Optional Field Breaks Serialization, and an Optional Parameter Can Still Be null

aspects.says: An Optional parameter has three states, and a caller can still pass null.
basis: section:An Optional Field Breaks Serialization, and an Optional Parameter Can Still Be null
aspects.reason: the failure is in the caller passing null, not in code the reader writes; the page shows the run

aspects.says: Java 8's other features are taught in their own units.
basis: section:The Rest of Java 8 Is Taught in Its Own Units
aspects.reason: a table of pointers to other units, which practise those features

aspects.says: A class doesn't inherit its interfaces' static methods: they are called on the interface, never through an implementer or an instance.
basis: section:Static Interface Methods Belong to the Interface: Implementers Don't Inherit Them

aspects.says: X.super.m() calls one interface's default, which keeps only that interface's promises, and reaches only a direct superinterface no other supertype extends.
basis: section:The JDK's New Defaults Reach Classes Written Before Them, and Two of Them Can Collide
aspects.reason: the difference shows only as spliterator characteristics and compile errors; the page shows the run, and the quiz checks the conflict that forces the choice
